SPECIFICATION FOR CHEESE HOOPS
0. FOR EWORD
standard have been given in this system.

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 September 1963, after the draft finalized by the Dairy Industry Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 The cheese hoop is used for moulding the curd and to hold it while it is being pressed in the vertical cheese press. 0.3 Wherever a reference to any Indian Standard appears in this specification, it shall be taken as a reference to the latest version of the standard. 0.4 Metric system has been adopted and all quantities and dimensions in India in this

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960 Rules for Rounding Off Numerical Values ( Revised). The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 0.6 This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions relating to cheese hoops, and it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes for cheese hoops for handling cheese respectively. 2. GENERAL DESCRIPTION the requirements 10 and 20 kg of

4.2 The handle and the hook attachments shall be made of stainless steel wires and sheets of designation 07Cr19Ni9 of IS : 1570-1961. 5. FABRICATION 5.1 The cylindrical rings may be either pressed to shape or butt welded. The upper ring shall slide smoothly and easily into the lower ring. The covers shall be pressed to shape and the perforations neatly and cleanly made. The cover for the upper ring may be pressed from one piece or may be made in two pieces with the component parts soundly butt welded. If butt welded, the joint shall be positioned as shown in the figure. The handle shall be soundly welded to the lower ring. The clamp for the hook attachments shall be soundly welded to the lower ring. The hook attachment shall be so designed that it may be smoothly and easily pushed in and out of the holes provided in the lower ring and provides ~proper support to the upper ring. Holes may be provided in the upper and the lower rings, if so desired by the purchaser. 6. FINISH 6.1 The component parts shall be smoothly finished ~free from sharp corners, burrs and sharp edges, and shall be well .polished. The, joints shall be sound and shall be free from crevicesand gaps which will render the hoops unhygienic. The welding shall be sound and free from porosity and brittleness. 3

2.1 The cheese hoop shall consist of two cylindrical rings which could be telescoped, and two perforated covers. The lower ring shall be fitted with hook attachments for supporting the upper ring. 3. DESIGN AND DIMENSK)NS

3.1 The cheese hoops shall generally conform to the shape and dimensions given in Fig. 1. 3.1.1 Dimensions given in the figure are only approximate and variations shall be permitted so long as the hoops conform to the general description, functian efficiently and are suitable for use in the cheese press conforming to IS : 2504-1963,Specification for Hand-Operated Cheese Press ( Vertical ). 4. MATERIALS 4.1 The cylindrical rings and the perforated covers shall be made of stainless steel sheets of designation 07Cr19Ni9 of Table XXXIV in IS : 1570-1961 Schedules for Wrought Steels for General Engineering Purposes.

Is : 2495 - 1963 7. MARKING 7.1 The cheese hoops shall be marked legibly and permanently with the following particulars: a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark or initials, if any; and b) Year of manufacture. 7.1.1 Each cheese hoop may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark.
NOTE - The use of the IS I Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark 01; products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a welldefined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may lx granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
